one_month_reasoning: No AppLovin earnings fall in Oct 2 - Oct 31: the company has not announced its Q3 date (it announced Q2's on Jul 1 for Aug 5), and third-party calendars put it at Nov 4-11; the lead-plaintiff deadline (Nov 16) is also outside. In-window items are second-order: the FOMC (Oct 27-28), Meta/Alphabet Q3 prints in late October (ad-market read-through), and more sell-side alt-data notes, which have moved the stock 3-13% in a day and have leaned negative. Offsetting: the stock sits at a 52-week low after a 7-session, 12% losing streak, with ~$1.8bn of buyback authorization and ~$3bn cash, and short-horizon reversal after a sharp selloff is a mild tailwind. These roughly cancel, so I center at about spot (median ~$282) with a ~20.5% monthly lognormal sigma (75% annual vol / 3.5, slightly trimmed): a near-symmetric spread, essentially unchanged from round 1.

Current EV ~$94.7bn (281.31 x 335M + $0.46bn net debt) is ~13.9x 2026E EBITDA of ~$6.8bn (Q1+Q2 reported $3.17bn + Q3 guide midpoint $1.725bn + Q4 ~$1.9bn) and ~11.5x consensus 2027 EBITDA (~$8.2bn); 13x on my lower 2027 number is in line with Piper's multiple compression.

bear.story: Model upgrades keep slipping and gaming share saturates (Edgewater); Unity Vector and Meta's AI game tools squeeze net-revenue spreads; e-commerce self-serve stalls (Wells Fargo pixel data); 2027 growth falls to ~10-15% and EPS ~$16-17; the class actions survive motions to dismiss and keep a governance discount. ~11x on ~$17 forward EPS. The SEC inquiry is closed, so a revived regulatory action is a tail inside this case, not its driver.

base.story: Growth slows to ~20% in 2027 as gaming matures and e-commerce ramps slowly (a 2027 story); margins ~80%; buybacks shrink the share count ~3%/yr; estimates drift ~5% lower, then stabilize; the multiple stays de-rated at ~14.5x forward EPS (~$21.5-22 NTM in Oct 2027).

bull.story: The post-quarter model step-up shows up in Q3/Q4 beats, e-commerce/self-serve Axon inflects in 2027, revisions turn positive, and the stock re-rates to ~19-20x on ~$24-25 forward EPS, still well below the $738 high.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$195 the stock would trade at ~10x my haircut FY2027 EPS ($19), ~8x EBITDA and a ~9.5% FCF yield, with only ~$0.46bn net debt, ~$3bn cash and a $1.8bn buyback authorization underneath. Sustained trading there would most likely mean the market expects earnings to fall, not just slower growth: a Q4 guide implying flat or negative q/q revenue, clear MAX/Axon share loss to Unity/Meta, an Apple/Google platform action on data practices, or a damaging litigation disclosure. Lowered from $205 because the SEC inquiry is closed; kept above the supervisor's $185 because the bear evidence (negative revisions, a first guidance miss, discretionary insider selling near the highs) is live.

reasoning: Lane: skeptic. Round 2 changes, from the supervisor's fact-checks and my follow-up: (a) Edgewater's Q4 call (+8-9% q/q, ~$2.25bn) is only ~1-2% below consensus, so my 8% FY27 EPS haircut double-counted it; I now cut 5% (Edgewater ~1-2% plus the Wells Fargo e-commerce delay and negative revisions), deeper than the supervisor's ~4% because revisions are still 19 down / 5 up. (b) The SEC inquiry is closed with no recommended action (CFO, Aug 5 2026, AdTechRadar), so I drop the regulatory component of the bear case and cut bear probability from 25% to 22%. (c) I disagree with the supervisor on the CEO's insider sales: the primary Form 4s for the Jun 10-12 2026 sales (104,166 shares, ~$51.1m at $473-517, part via children's trusts) have the Rule 10b5-1 checkbox unticked and no 10b5-1 footnote, and the matching Form 144s carry no plan remark, whereas director Vivas's March Form 144 explicitly cites a 10b5-1 plan dated 12/10/2025. The supervisor's source was a paywalled MarketScreener summary I could not read. So my round-1 fact stands, but I give it little price weight: it matters for the class action's scienter element, not for earnings. Valuation: P/E $323 (19.0 x 17x), FCF yield $311, EV/EBITDA $309; blended fair value $315 (from $306). Scenarios: bear $190 (22%), base $315 (53%), bull $480 (25%); mean ~$329, median ~$305. Ladder: average of a three-scenario lognormal mixture (inner sigmas 30-35%) and a single lognormal (median ~$302, sigma 0.62, below the 75% realized vol because that vol includes a one-off de-rating), which keeps fat tails. Result: P(>= $281) ~0.57 (from 0.55), ~20% chance below $197, ~5.5% chance above $703. Thesis break $195 (from $205). Research limited (paywalls, 403s); no options data or priors consulted.
